becomes:
/* SIZE 8 KEEPS ITS LINES WHOLE (patch614; on every picture since round 6).

   The owner, on the size-8 results for mouths, eyes and chains: "even
   when using 8 its not good but fix it for 8 then". At a step of exactly
   8 px the engine runs PF.repair8_pack (pixelfixer/src/pf-42-repair8.js):
   a line one cell wide that falls across two cells goes to one of them
   instead of vanishing or doubling (Mouth 05's teeth bars), a thin stroke
   stays connected, and a speck of noise in a flat fill takes the fill's
   colour. On every picture, from any folder or none: the owner,
   2026-10-01, "i dont want specific rules for certain traits, i just want
   it to funnction so that those rules dont need to be in place". Where a
   rule went wrong on a picture it was never measured on, the rule now
   tells from the picture (the module's header, round 6).
   Superseded: a list of three layers (mouth, eyes, chains) and
   fixRepair8(step,rel) - only those layers, and a file with no layer in
   its path kept today's cells. */
function fixRepair8(step){
  return step===8;
}
/* AT PIXEL SIZE 16 A LINE THINNER THAN A CELL STAYS A LINE (round 3; gate
   guard round 4; rim guards round 5; every picture round 6).

   At a step of exactly 16 px (80 cells on the 1280 canvas) a drawn line
   thinner than a cell loses the cell vote to the fill on either side and
   comes out as dots or not at all: Dogecoin Polo's collar, GATE Hoodie's
   white outline round its letters, Circuit Board Skin's gold traces, the
   black outline of Noun Glasses (gone entirely). The engine then runs
   PF.lines16_pack (pixelfixer/src/pf-42-repair8.js): a line on a fill is
   joined across its gaps, a line straddling two cells goes to the one
   holding its centre, and neither may take a cell of the shape the line
   outlines (GATE's yellow letters stay yellow) or fill a hole in the art.
   On every picture, from any folder or none (the owner, 2026-10-01, as for
   size 8). Superseded: a list of nine layers (round 5, never live) -
   backgrounds, chains, mouths and eyes kept today's cells. */
function fixLines16(step){
  return step===16;
}
/* THE OUTLINE GATE, SENT WITH THE SIZE-8 AND SIZE-16 RULES WHEN THE PASS WILL
   RUN (fixOutlineRuns: the switch is on and the mode makes cells; since round 6
   no layer decides, so there is no picture to ask about), else null. The rules may not switch the
   pass on or off for a shape (round 4): a few black cells added to an edge
   can tip a shape over the pass's "half its edge is black" test, and the
   pass then repaints the whole shape's edge - Desert Jedi Robes: 2 cells
   added, the dark-brown sleeve's edge painted black and its shading
   peeled. The worker's guard asks the pass's own question with the pass's
   own numbers (OUTLINE_GATE), not a copy. */
function fixLines16Gate(){
  return fixOutlineRuns() ? OUTLINE_GATE : null;
}

Without opts.source both are off and the pass is byte-identical to before (424/424 runs).
   [D1] A SMALL DRAWING IS NOT THINNED (round 7, 2026-10-01). A selected part whose cells cover less than MIN_THIN_PX =
        32,000 source px (cells x cell size squared; 500 cells at size 8, 2,000 at 4, 320 at 10, none at 16 where the
        gate's 200 cells is already 51,200 px) keeps every black cell it has: no peel (it is treated as [M1]'s
        noPeel) and no whisker cut. Its ring is still made black where it is dark or has a gap (step 2), so a
        chain's or pendant's outline is still made whole. Why: once the pass ran on every picture (round 6), the
        peel and the whisker cut removed black that is the drawing in mouths, eyes and pendants - the Smoking
        Pipe's rim spike and the dark row under its rim, the Pill on Tongue lip edge drawn 2 cells wide, Golden
        Swarm's and XRP's link black, the eyes' 2-cell lines at size 4, Joint Behind Ear's tip block. Measured
        first (scratchpad fix8/round7/outline7, notes.txt): no test on the cells or the source pixels tells those
        from what the pass thins on the 212 traits it covered before - the Navy Double Symbol Cap's dark-navy
        row behind its black line is the pipe's dark row (both a near-black colour, a whole source block, one
        block behind the line, on an 8 px art grid the cells reproduce exactly); its 2-block stair steps are the
        pipe bowl's; the spiky hair's whiskers are as solid in the source as the pipe's spike. What separates
        them is the size of the drawing: at sizes 4, 8, 10 and 16 every part that lost drawn black covers 31,328
        source px or less, and every part of the 212 the pass thins at size 8, 10 or 16 covers 32,640 or more,
        except Bonk Impact's biggest exclamation mark (13,120 px at size 8), which now stays as drawn like its
        two smaller marks (the gate's 200 cells never reached those). At size 4 two parts of the 212 now keep
        their line too: a Cyan Battle Axe part (9,840 px) and Among Us Shoulder Crewmate (31,664). The margin is
        small (Among Us: 32,640 px at size 8) and a new trait near the line can fall either side - this is a
        size rule, chosen on these 311, and says so.
